# Periodically validate the human experience against the intended experience

> **Headline:** Add a versioned, bot-baseline-derived **intended-experience
> targets** artifact plus a deterministic **human-experience validation**
> command that compares measured human (and bot) balance statistics against
> those bands, emitting a versioned JSON report and Markdown summary and
> failing with a non-zero exit code on drift.

**Priority:** medium · **Issue type:** feature · **Assignee:** Map

## Problem statement

Balancing is currently a manual, point-in-time activity. The automated-balancing
framework produces a stable, versioned `BalanceReport`, and the human-play
statistics work item produces the *same* statistics for real players — but
nothing states what the experience is *supposed* to be, and nothing periodically
checks the measured experience against it. This item turns the bot batch into
the **source of truth for intended experience** (recorded as explicit target
bands and mirrored into the GDD), then adds a repeatable validation that flags
drift in the measured human experience.

## Users

- **As a game designer / producer**, I want a periodic report comparing the
  measured human experience against explicit intended-experience targets, so I
  can see whether the game still plays as designed and where it has drifted.
- **As a game designer / maintainer**, I want the intended experience written
  down as machine-checkable targets derived from a bot baseline, so a tuning
  change can be judged against a recorded standard rather than remembered.
- **As a maintainer**, I want the same validation to run against a fresh bot
  batch, so a regression in the balance baseline is caught even before any human
  play is recorded.
- **As a producer**, I want a durable, versioned pass/fail artifact, so the
  experience of the game can be reviewed over time.

## Intended-experience definition (decision recorded)

The operator chose the **bot baseline** as the source of intended-experience
targets, with the **GDD updated to match**. Concretely:

- A bot batch (`npm run evaluate -- --batch`) produces the shared
  `BalanceAggregate`. Its per-metric distributions define the **target band**
  (centre = baseline mean/median; tolerance = a documented multiple of std-dev
  or a relative percentage).
- The resulting bands are committed as a **versioned targets artifact** — the
  single machine-checkable statement of intended experience.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` is updated so the *prose* intended experience
  (survival, pacing, progression, reward cadence) agrees with those bands.

This keeps one source of truth (the artifact) and one narrative (the GDD).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Versioned, machine-checkable targets.** A targets artifact (e.g.
   `src/data/experience-targets.json`) records, for each key metric of the
   shared `BalanceAggregate` schema — at minimum `survivalSeconds`,
   `mineralsCollected`, `upgradesSelected`, `waveReached`, `levelReached` and
   `avoidableHits` — a target band (centre + tolerance) plus a version
   constant, seeded from a recorded bot batch baseline. A test asserts the
   artifact validates against the schema and covers every required metric.
- **Pure comparator.** A pure, clock-free, I/O-free module compares a
   `BalanceAggregate` (human **or** bot) against the targets and returns, per
   metric, the measured value, the target band, the signed drift magnitude and
   a pass/fail verdict. Unit tests cover in-band, above-band, below-band,
   missing-metric and empty-input cases, and assert no I/O / clock access.
- **Periodic validation command.** A documented on-demand command (e.g.
   `npm run validate-experience -- <balance-report.json>`) reads a
   `BalanceReport`, compares it against the targets, writes a **versioned JSON
   report** and a **Markdown summary**, and **exits non-zero when any metric
   drifts beyond tolerance**. It labels the source (human / bot policy) in the
   output. Its scheduling (e.g. a documented cron/CI recipe) is documented but
   not built as CI infrastructure in this item.
- **Determinism and reproducibility.** The same input report + targets yields
   byte-identical JSON and Markdown output; the pure core never reads the wall
   clock. Verified by tests (run twice, diff).
- **GDD, documentation and test suite.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` is
   updated so the intended experience matches the bot-baseline-derived targets;
   the validation workflow, targets artifact and report shape are documented
   (extending `docs/BALANCING.md` and/or a new `docs/EXPERIENCE_VALIDATION.md`
   plus code comments/README as applicable); and the **full project test suite
   passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Delivered dependency:** this item depends on **Collect balance statistics
  from human player games (dev mode only)** (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN), which is
  now **completed**, together with its helper child AH-0MV8ISO4O002HHDT
  (`src/ai/eval/humanStats.ts` exists). The human `BalanceReport` this
  validation consumes is therefore available; implementation may proceed.
- Reuse the shared schema (`BALANCE_STATISTICS_SCHEMA_VERSION`,
  `BalanceRunStats`, `BalanceAggregate`, `BalanceReport`) — no schema
  duplication.
- **Dev tooling only:** the targets artifact and validator are development
  tooling; no production game-code call site, no telemetry/consent change.
- Deterministic and byte-stable output; the pure core must not read the wall
  clock or perform I/O.
- No wall-clock/network dependency in the comparator; the `--batch` path is
  already reproducible and must stay so.

## Existing state

- **Shared schema:** `src/ai/eval/types.ts` defines `DistributionStats`,
  `BalanceRunStats`, `BalanceAggregate`, `BalanceReport`,
  `BALANCE_STATISTICS_SCHEMA_VERSION` and `EVAL_DATASET_VERSION`
  (AH-0MV81YJQP008L9CQ, completed).
- **Bot batch:** `src/ai/eval/engine.ts` + `scripts/evaluate.mjs` write a
  byte-stable `balance-report.json` / `.txt` / `runs.jsonl` under `--out`
  (default `eval-output/`), documented in `docs/BALANCING.md`. A recorded
  100-game baseline exists in that document's acceptance-verification section.
- **Human stats (delivered):** **Collect balance statistics from human
  player games** (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN, completed) emits a `BalanceReport`
  labelled with a `human` pseudo-policy. Its helper
  (`src/ai/eval/humanStats.ts`, AH-0MV8ISO4O002HHDT) is present.
- **No targets, comparator or validation command exists today.**
- **Related tuning loop:** **Automate the balance-tuning loop** (
  AH-0MV8Q5EYE001R715, open) covers baseline/compare for *tuning*; this item
  covers *periodic experience validation* against a committed standard.

## Desired change

1. Add a versioned targets artifact (schema + initial bot-baseline values) and
   a loader/validator.
2. Add a pure comparator module producing per-metric drift + verdicts.
3. Add the validation CLI and a `package.json` script.
4. Add the JSON + Markdown report writers (byte-stable).
5. Add tests (schema, comparator, CLI, determinism) and update docs + GDD.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ai/eval/types.ts` — add target/drift types + version constant (or a new
  `experienceTargets.ts`).
- `src/ai/eval/experienceTargets.ts` — pure targets loader + comparator
  (new).
- `src/data/experience-targets.json` — versioned intended-experience bands
  seeded from a bot baseline (new; exact path TBD at implementation).
- `src/ai/eval/experienceTargets.test.ts` — schema + comparator unit tests
  (new).
- `scripts/validate-experience.mjs` (+ `.d.mts`) — validation CLI (new).
- `scripts/validate-experience.test.ts` — CLI + determinism tests (new).
- `package.json` — add the validation script.
- `docs/EXPERIENCE_VALIDATION.md` and/or `docs/BALANCING.md` — document the
  workflow, targets and report shape.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — align the stated intended experience with
  the targets.

## Related work

- **Automated Balancing** (AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW) — epic that delivered the
  schema and batch runner.
- **Collect balance statistics from human player games (dev mode only)**
  (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN) — supplies the human statistics (dependency).
- **Shared human balance-statistics helper** (AH-0MV8ISO4O002HHDT) — the
  helper this item depends on indirectly.
- **Balance statistics schema and pure aggregation** (AH-0MV81YJQP008L9CQ) —
  the shared schema.
- **Automate the balance-tuning loop: baseline, single-edit, re-run and diff**
  (AH-0MV8Q5EYE001R715) — related baseline/compare tooling.
- Docs: `docs/BALANCING.md`, `docs/EVALUATION.md`,
  `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/TELEMETRY.md`.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the bot batch is a *directional* proxy for the human
  experience (documented fidelity boundary in `docs/BALANCING.md`). Target
  bands are therefore intentionally tolerant; an out-of-band *human* result is
  a prompt to investigate, not proof of a bug.
- **Risk (dependency):** implementation is blocked until the human-stats item
  lands; the brief can be finalised now but must not proceed to implementation.
- **Risk (target inflation):** deriving targets from the bot baseline makes the
  bot trivially self-consistent; the comparator's value is against *human*
  stats. Document this explicitly so a green bot run is not mistaken for proof
  of a good human experience.
- **Risk (tolerance tuning):** too-tight bands cause false drift alarms; too
  loose hide real regressions. Mitigation: state the tolerance rule in the
  artifact and document how to adjust it.
- **Scope-creep risk:** CI scheduling, dashboards and automatic ticket creation
  on drift are *out of scope*; scheduling is documented only.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Where should the initial *intended-experience targets* come from?**
  — Answer (operator, interactive): **Bot baseline, and update the GDD to
  match.** The bot batch's aggregate distributions define the target bands; the
  GDD is edited so its prose intended experience agrees. Source: interactive
  reply.
- **Q: What form should the "periodic" run take?**
  — Answer (operator): **As recommended** — an on-demand, deterministic
  validation command with documented scheduling (no CI cron infra is added in
  this item; the repo has none today). Source: interactive reply.
- **Q: What should the validation emit?**
  — Answer (operator): **Versioned JSON + Markdown summary + exit code**
  (non-zero on drift). Source: interactive reply.
- **Q: What is the current state of the shared schema and human stats?**
  — Answer (agent, research): The shared schema is delivered
  (`src/ai/eval/types.ts`, AH-0MV81YJQP008L9CQ); the human-stats collection is
  still open (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN) and its helper
  (`src/ai/eval/humanStats.ts`, AH-0MV8ISO4O002HHDT) does not exist. This item
  is consequently `blocked` for implementation. Research: `wl show` +
  `ls src/ai/eval/`. Source: repository.
- **Q: Does a targets artifact or validator already exist?**
  — Answer (agent, research): No. Research: `ls src/ai/eval/`, `grep` of
  `docs/BALANCING.md`. Source: repository.

**Revision (plan review):** The human-stats dependency
(AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN) and its helper (AH-0MV8ISO4O002HHDT) are now
**completed** (`src/ai/eval/humanStats.ts` present). The earlier "blocked"
constraint above is superseded by this revision; planning proceeded on the
now-unblocked content. Re-verified that no targets artifact
(`src/data/experience-targets.json`) and no validation CLI
(`scripts/validate-experience.mjs`) exist yet.

## Plan: changelog

- Plan review auto-complete path (effort Small / risk Low, below the
  decomposition threshold): six automated review stages run against existing
  content, AC coverage review returned `proceed`. Corrections applied:
  dependency status refreshed from `blocked` to `delivered` in Constraints,
  Existing state, and the Appendix. No feature children created — the item is
  a single small, well-defined vertical slice suitable for direct
  implementation.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW** – Automated Balancing (completed)
- **AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN** – Collect balance statistics from human player games (dev mode only) (open)
- **AH-0MV8ISO4O002HHDT** – Shared human balance-statistics helper (blocked)

# Enemies should be aware of the wrap around

## Problem statement

Enemies are currently "wrap-blind": aimed shots always fire a straight line at
the player's raw position (never crossing a screen edge), and enemy movement is
bounded or clamped to the arena, so no enemy ever flies over a screen edge the
way the player ship, asteroids, bullets and the raider patrol already do. The
playfield seam is therefore one-directional — only the player's shots and the
player can cross it — letting the player camp the edges with impunity. Enemy
behaviour should be wrap-aware by default — firing across the seam to reach the
player and flying over the edges — controlled by a per-enemy parameter so a
small set of classic arcade archetypes (Space Invaders march, Centipede) keeps
its bounded, wall-respecting behaviour.

## Users

- **Players** — enemy shots can now arrive from anywhere, including from
  "off-screen" across the seam, so camping a screen edge is no longer a safe
  position. Most enemies occupy the whole wrap-around world rather than a
  bounded box, while the classic set pieces (Space Invaders, Centipede) stay
  recognisible.
- **AI agents / human developers** — one unambiguous data-driven per-archetype
  parameter (`wrapAware`, default `true`) that the game and every gym read
  through the same shared seams, so game↔gym parity is preserved by
  construction and tuning an archetype is a one-field change.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want enemies to fire at me across the screen edge, so that
  hiding against an edge is no longer a guaranteed safe position and shots can
  arrive from the seam exactly like my own wrapped bullets.
- As a **player**, I want most enemies to fly over a screen edge and reappear on
  the opposite side, so the whole wrapped playfield — not a bounded box — is
  part of the arena.
- As a **player**, I want the Space Invaders block and the Centipede to keep
  their classic behaviour (reversing at the walls / weaving within the arena),
  so those recognisable set pieces remain intact.
- As a **developer**, I want a single data-driven `wrapAware` parameter per
  archetype (default: aware) that behaves identically in the game and every
  gym, so enabling or disabling seam-awareness is a one-field change with no
  divergent copies.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Parameter** — Each enemy archetype carries a data-driven boolean
   `wrapAware` (or equivalently named) parameter, defaulting to `true`, wired
   through the existing `EnemyConfig` pipeline so it is visible and editable in
   the enemy editor panel. The `march` (Space Invaders) and `centipede` seed
   configs set it to `false`.
2. **Seam-aware aimed fire** — Aimed shots (Scout, march and the raider's
   aimed fire — every archetype routed through the aimed-shot method) fire
   along the shortest wrapped path to the player: when the direct line is
   longer than the wrap-around route, the shot leaves one edge and arrives from
   the opposite edge (enemy bullets already wrap; AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0). An
   enemy with `wrapAware: false` keeps the current direct aim.
3. **Wrap-aware movement** — Wrap-aware enemy motion (dive, chase, orbit,
   drift, roam, hold-and-move, etc.) that would carry the enemy off-screen
   wraps to the opposite edge (matching the player/asteroid four-edge wrap
   model) instead of being clamped. Non-aware archetypes (`march`,
   `centipede`) are unchanged: march reverses and drops at the arena edge;
   centipede weaves within bounds.
4. **Gym ↔ game parity** — The behaviour is implemented once in the shared
   core (`src/scenes/core/`) and exercised by the affected gym scene(s) and
   `PlayScene` in the same change, so the repo-wide duplicate-body / parity
   guards stay green.
5. **Testing, validation & docs** — Unit tests cover: seam-aware aim angle for
   wrap-aware enemies vs. direct aim for non-aware enemies; position wrapping
   on crossing each edge for wrap-aware motion; config default / CSV wiring
   including the `march` / `centipede` exclusions. The affected documentation
   (`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` and any config-format docs) is
   updated to reflect the change. The full project test suite passes with the
   new changes.

## Constraints

- Do not change the bullet wrap model itself — enemy bullets already wrap and
  expire by lifetime (AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0); this item changes launch direction
  and enemy movement only.
- Exclusions are an explicit seed-config list: only `march` and `centipede`
  default to non-aware. During planning, any other archetype whose classic
  design requires wall interaction belongs in the exclusion list, recorded as a
  code comment and a documented divergence per the gym↔game parity convention
  (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1).
- Implement through the shared core (`src/scenes/core/`), never a divergent
  copy, so the game and every gym run the same code.
- Out of scope: boss behaviours, player ship, minerals, drops, and the bullet
  wrap model itself.
- Written in UK English per repo convention.

## Existing state

- Enemy aimed fire: `Scout.tryFireAimedBullet` computes
  `heading = atan2(target.y - y, target.x - x)` on **raw** positions with no
  seam consideration — the same aimed-shot method is reused for march and
  raider via `ENEMY_FIRE_METHODS` (`src/entities/enemyFire.ts`).
- Enemy bullets: wrap all four screen edges and expire by lifetime
  (AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0; shared bullet path in `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts`).
- Enemy movement: bounded. Ghost/Grunt clamp to `GAME_WIDTH`/`GAME_HEIGHT`;
  march reverses and drops at arena bounds (`src/scenes/core/marchFormation.ts`:
  `computeMarchBounds` / `advanceMarch`); centipede weaves within bounds;
  formation drift pushes rightward.
- Wrap model to match: player ship and `Asteroid.updatePosition` four-edge
  wrap; `Raider` patrol already wraps; `LaneTraffic` wraps horizontally.
- Enemies are data-driven: `EnemyConfig` (`src/core/configTypes.ts`) + seed
  defaults (`src/core/configDefaults.ts`) + CSV (`src/data/enemy-configs.csv`)
  + enemy editor panel + gym editor.

## Desired change

1. Add the boolean parameter to `EnemyConfig` (`wrapAware`), seed default
   `true`; set `march` and `centipede` to `false`.
2. Seam-aware aim: for wrap-aware entities, compute the player delta along the
   shortest wrapped path before `atan2` in the shared aimed-fire seam; used by
   Scout / march / raider aimed fire (and any other archetype sharing the
   aimed-shot method).
3. Shared post-motion edge wrap: in the shared scene entity loop (game +
   gyms), wrap each wrap-aware enemy's position when it crosses an edge; gate
   on the flag so non-aware archetypes are untouched.
4. Verify per-archetype that nothing breaks (divers mid-dive, chasers,
   orbiters, swarm, formation drift) and adjust tests.
5. Update key docs (`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`; config-format
   docs if they enumerate fields).

## Key Files

- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — add `wrapAware?: boolean` to `EnemyConfig`.
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts` — seed defaults: `true` for most archetypes;
  `false` for `march` and `centipede`.
- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` — new `wrapAware` column entries (if the CSV
  persists the field).
- `src/entities/enemyFire.ts` + aimed-fire call sites (`Scout.tryFireAimedBullet`,
  march, `Raider`) — seam-aware aim.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — expose the flag and any shared seam support.
- `src/scenes/core/` — shared post-motion wrap (CombatCoreScene / CombatScene
  shared entity loop, alongside the `enemyTargeting.ts` seams).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` + affected gym scenes
  (`GymFodderEnemies`, `GymCentipede`, …) — parity exercises.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — document the parameter and the
  exclusions.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: gameplay feel** — seam-aware aimed fire lets shots come from
  unexpected directions; mitigated by limiting the change to aimed shots
  (radial/spread remain direction-symmetric) and excluding the classic
  archetypes.
- **Risk: wrap × state-machine interaction** — a post-motion wrap applied to
  every wrap-aware archetype could interact with steering that seeks the player
  or with dive/common state machines near the seam (oscillation). Mitigation:
  per-archetype verification during planning and dedicated unit tests at the
  seam.
- **Risk: formation-drift scope** — drift formations that push off-screen wrap
  at the entity level; formation *bases* and shaping logic stay as-is.
- **Scope-creep guard** — seam-aware spread/radial patterns (Q2 option b) are
  out of scope; if wanted later they are tracked as a new work item, not added
  here. Any extra archetype exclusion discovered during planning becomes a new
  work item or is documented as a divergence, not silent scope growth.
- **Assumption: config plumbing** — the parameter lives in `EnemyConfig`
  (CSV-backed, editor-editable), consistent with the established data-driven
  enemy tooling; default `true` for all archetypes except the explicit
  exclusions.

## Related work

- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** — "Bullets should have a distance and should wrap
  around the screen" (completed). Bullets already wrap; this item builds
  directly on that model for launch direction.
- **AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW** — "Enemies should emerge from the wormhole" (open).
  Touches the same shared enemy spawn/motion seams; potential overlap to watch
  during planning.
- **AH-0MU4KQ6NT006MP52** — "Extract common enemy base class for regular
  enemies" (completed). `BaseEnemy` hosts the shared config/seam support.
- **AH-0MTFP7EIC004F1MN** — "Enemy Design tooling" (completed). The
  data-driven `EnemyConfig` pipeline this parameter extends.
- **AH-0MTAN4X5D009D7U6** — "Write ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md
  best-practice guide" (completed). The doc updated by AC 5.
- **AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1** — gym↔game parity convention (referenced in
  `AGENTS.md`), enforced by `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Movement scope: which enemies should actually 'fly over the edge'? (a)
  All wrap-aware archetypes — shared post-motion wrap in scene loops;
  march/centipede excluded. (b) Firing only. (c) A curated subset."
  — Answer (Map): "(a)". Source: interactive reply, intake round 1.
- Q2: "Firing scope: which fire patterns become seam-aware? (a) Aimed shots
  only. (b) All patterns."
  — Answer (Map): "(a)". Source: interactive reply, intake round 1.

# Test: wrap-aware enemy movement

Test-first verification slice for wrap-aware movement (parent AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8, AC3 + AC5). Pins per-edge wrapping for wrap-aware archetypes and the unchanged bounded behaviour of the classic exclusions.

## Goal

Specify, in tests, that wrap-aware motion which would carry an enemy off-screen wraps to the opposite edge while `march` and `centipede` keep their bounded, wall-respecting behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Tests assert that crossing each of the four edges (left, right, top, bottom) relocates a wrap-aware enemy to the opposite edge, matching the player/asteroid four-edge wrap model (position only — velocity preserved).
- Tests cover the shared post-motion wrap helper in isolation (pure function, no Phaser) including the exact-boundary and multi-edge-overshoot cases.
- A test asserts `march` still reverses at the arena edge and drops vertically, and that `centipede` still weaves within bounds (`src/scenes/core/marchFormation.ts` / centipede formation unchanged).
- A regression test asserts a non-aware archetype's position is never wrapped by the shared seam even when it leaves the arena bounds.
- At least one test covers each wrap-aware movement class (dive, chase, orbit, drift, roam, hold-and-move) at the seam.
- All tests pass deterministically.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/marchFormation.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`
- `src/entities/Ghost.test.ts`
- `src/entities/Asteroid.test.ts`

## Acceptance Criteria

- The tests fail against the pre-change bounded/clamped motion and pass once the shared wrap lands.

# Implement: shared post-motion edge wrap

Implementation slice for wrap-aware movement (parent AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8, AC3). One shared post-motion step wraps wrap-aware enemies across the seam instead of clamping them to the arena.

## Goal

Wrap each wrap-aware enemy's position in the shared scene entity loop (game + gyms), gated on `wrapAware`, so the whole wrapped playfield is the arena for every archetype except the classic exclusions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single shared post-motion wrap step lives in `src/scenes/core/` and is called from the shared entity loop used by both `PlayScene` and the gym scenes — no per-scene or per-entity copy.
- Wrap-aware enemies (dive, chase, orbit, drift, roam, hold-and-move) wrap across the opposite edge when their motion would carry them off-screen; velocity and heading are preserved (no reflection).
- `march` and `centipede` remain unchanged: march reverses and drops at the arena edge, centipede weaves within bounds.
- Formation bases and formation-shaping logic are unchanged — wrapping is entity-level only (per parent risk note).
- Steering that seeks the player remains stable near the seam (no oscillation); the shared wrap does not fight a steering state machine.
- No archetype other than the documented exclusions keeps bounded/clamped motion; any extra exclusion discovered is recorded as a code comment plus a documented divergence.
- Build passes and the changed-scope tests (including the slice-5 tests) are green.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/enemyTargeting.ts`
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`
- `src/entities/Ghost.ts`
- `src/entities/Grunt.ts`

# Test: gym-game parity for wrap behaviour

Test-first verification slice for gym↔game parity (parent AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8, AC4 + AC5). Extends the repo-wide duplicate-body/parity guards to cover wrap-aware aim and motion so the game and every gym cannot drift.

## Goal

Prove, by test, that wrap-aware aim and movement run the *same* code in `PlayScene` and the affected gym scenes, and that the equivalence guards cover the new seams.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The parity/equivalence guard (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) covers the seam-aware aim and post-motion wrap seams and stays green.
- A cross-scene test asserts a wrap-aware aimed shot produces the same launch angle in the affected gym scene(s) and `PlayScene` for identical geometry.
- A cross-scene test asserts the post-motion wrap relocated position is identical in the affected gym scene(s) and `PlayScene`.

## Problem statement

The PlayScene integration test `PlayScene — Robotron homing horde (AH-0MV01EKTL001NRE6) > killing a grunt advances wave accounting exactly once` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`) failed once during the AI_Hell full suite (heavy machine load) and passed on a fresh full-suite re-run minutes later with identical code. It is a flaky test, not a gameplay regression, and it is the last remaining kill test in this file that has not been hardened against non-deterministic scene state.

## Users

- **AI agents and producers running the full suite** — a red full-suite gate blocks `dev` pushes and triggers `test-failure` triage items and retries.
- **Developers of the Robotron horde (and shared kill seam)** — they need the horde kill/accounting contract to stay proven while the test stays stable.

Example user stories:

- *As an agent whose `implement.py finish` gate runs the full suite, I want the Robotron horde kill test to pass deterministically so that an unrelated docs-only change is never blocked by it.*
- *As a maintainer, I want the wave-accounting contract (a horde kill counted exactly once) still asserted, so the fix does not hide a real regression.*

## Existing state (evidence)

Failure from the `implement.py finish` gate for AH-0MVLJFCE6007T77H (docs-only change, cannot affect kill behaviour):

```
FAIL |integration| src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — Robotron homing horde > killing a grunt advances wave accounting exactly once
AssertionError: expected true to be false // Object.is equality
 ❯ src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:6168:26
    6166|     scene.spawnPlayerBullet(victim.x, victim.y, 0, 0);
    6167|     scene.tick(0.001);
    6168|     expect(victim.alive).toBe(false);
```

Same run also printed repeated `connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:3000` on stderr (unrelated noise; no test failed on it).

The current test body (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:6174-6184`) is:

```ts
const victim = liveGrunts(scene)[0];
scene.spawnPlayerBullet(victim.x, victim.y, 0, 0);
scene.tick(0.001);
expect(victim.alive).toBe(false);
expect(wm.enemiesAlive).toBe(total - 1);
```

Two facts narrow the cause:

1. **The test is non-deterministic per run, independent of load.** `bootWithHordeWave()` never injects an RNG or run seed, so `PlayScene._initRunSeed()` draws a fresh `randomSeed()` (`Math.random()`, `src/core/rng.ts`) each run and the horde plan (`computeHordeSpawns`, `src/waves/HordeSpawner.ts`) places the 16 grunts at RNG-jittered points along the four arena edges. The passing re-run therefore re-drew a different layout; "passed on re-run" is *not* evidence that load is the variable.
2. **The identical scenario has already been fixed one describe-block earlier.** `killing a pursuer advances wave accounting exactly once` (Pac-Man pursuer) had the same single-`tick(0.001)` shape and the same flake, and was fixed by wrapping the kill in the existing module-level `isolateEnemyForKill(scene, victim)` helper (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:397-410`, documented as AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK): it stubs `getEnemyEntities()` to the victim only and disables auto-fire for the duration, so "auto-fire or an overlapping pursuer cannot add a second kill and double-decrement the wave accounting". The Robotron horde kill test is the *unhardened sibling* of that test — it predates/omits the isolation.

The description's original hypothesis ("the physics/collision step for that tick may not process the new projectile before the assertion") is **not** supported: `scene.tick(dt)` is a synchronous call that runs the full player/auto-fire/bullet/collision/accounting pass in one go (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:1265+`), so a longer tick cannot make a pass "complete"; what changes with a longer tick is *how much extra state* (auto-fire bullets, homing movement, wave timer) participates in that pass.

## Diagnosis to confirm during implementation

Confirm the exact mechanism before changing the assertion. Candidate mechanisms, in order of likelihood:

1. **Auto-fire / other-bullet interference** — the scene's auto-fire is live in this scenario, so a shot fired in the same tick can hit a grunt (or a different, overlapping grunt) and shift which entity the spawned bullet resolves against. The pursuer precedent (AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK) fixed exactly this with `isolateEnemyForKill`.
2. **Overlapping horde grunts** — grunts in one spawn group share an edge and can be placed close enough that a bullet placed on the victim is also within an earlier-iterated grunt's hit radius.
3. **Wave-phase/`paused` gating** — a wave-timeout transition switches `tick()` to the carried-survivor-only collision pass (`_handleCarriedSurvivorCollisions`), and a paused scene makes `tick()` a no-op; either would leave the victim alive. Check `scene.isTransitioning()` / `paused` under the failing seed.
4. **Wall-clock frames before the loop is stopped** — `bootScene()` resumes the live RAF loop, and `advanceGame()` stops it only after a microtask yield, so real frames with real deltas run before the deterministic stepping begins (load-dependent state drift). Relevant if the failure reproduces without seed isolation.

Reproduce deterministically (seed sweep): inject a fixed seed via `scene.setRng(createSeededRng(<seed>))` before `scene.restart()` and sweep seeds until the failure reproduces, then fix and verify that seed. Prefer the narrowest fix that removes the interference.

Steps to reproduce (seed sweep):

1. In `bootWithHordeWave()`, add `scene.setRng(createSeededRng(seed))` before `scene.scene.restart()` (import `createSeededRng` from `../core/rng`).
2. Loop seeds (e.g. `0..999`) in a temporary harness or repeated test-skill runs until `victim.alive` is `true` after the kill step; note the seed.
3. Record the seed and the observed mechanism on this work item, then apply the fix and re-verify that seed plus a broader sweep.

## Desired change

Make the horde kill test deterministic **without weakening what it proves**:

- Isolate the kill exactly as the pursuer test does — reuse `isolateEnemyForKill(scene, victim)` (`auto-fire` off, only the victim visible to the collision pass) — and/or pin the scene RNG to a fixed seed so the horde layout is reproducible.
- Keep the single-tick kill if it is deterministic after isolation; otherwise use a small bounded "tick until the victim dies" loop (guard counter, e.g. ≤ 20 frames of `0.016`) and assert the *outcome*.
- Still assert that the victim dies **and** that wave accounting drops by exactly one — and, to prove "exactly once", assert the accounting is unchanged after further ticks (no double decrement).

## Acceptance criteria

- The flaky failure is reproduced deterministically first (fixed seed and/or a temporary repeat-run harness), and the observed mechanism is recorded as a comment on this work item with the failing seed (or an explicit statement that no seed reproduces it, with the evidence gathered).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — Robotron homing horde > killing a grunt advances wave accounting exactly once` passes on repeated runs: at least 20 consecutive runs of `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` via the test skill, and at least one run with an additional concurrent load-generating job active, all green.
- The test still proves the contract: the victim grunt is dead after the kill step, and `wm.enemiesAlive` is exactly `total - 1` (and stays `total - 1` after further ticks — a kill is never counted twice). The "exactly once" proof is not weakened to "at most once".
- The fix is confined to test code (plus test comments); no gameplay behaviour, RNG semantics, or `isSpawning`/collision logic changes. If investigation shows a genuine gameplay defect is being masked, stop and record it as a new work item (`discovered-from:AH-0MVMEI9V1005H0LU`) rather than loosening the test.
- If the fix pattern is reusable (e.g. other horde/pursuer kill tests), note it in the test comment referencing AH-0MVMEI9V1005H0LU and AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK so the next reader sees why the isolation is required.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Test-execution policy:** every agent-initiated test run goes through the test skill (`/skill:test`, `run_tests.py`) — no ad-hoc `vitest`/`npm test`. Repeated-run verification is therefore a test-skill invocation with a narrow scope (changed-scope gate) plus the full-suite gate at push.
- **No assertion weakening:** a longer tick alone is acceptable only if it is deterministic after isolation; it must not become a "sleep until it works" loop with an unbounded guard.
- **No production-code behaviour change:** the horde kill path (`_resolvePlayerBulletsVsEnemies`, `onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy`) is shared with every gym (`src/scenes/core/`), so a behavioural change would require gym-parity work — out of scope unless a real defect is found.
- Prefer reusing existing helpers (`isolateEnemyForKill`, `finishSpawnSequence`) over introducing a new pattern.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — horde kill test at ~6174; `bootWithHordeWave`/`releaseHorde` helpers at ~6089-6124; existing `isolateEnemyForKill` helper at ~397-410 to reuse.
- `src/waves/HordeSpawner.ts` — RNG-driven spawn placement (`computeHordeSpawns`) explaining per-run layout variance.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `planHordeSpawns` / `_releaseDueHordeSpawns` (~2164-2245), `tick` collision/phase ordering (~1265-1390), `_initRunSeed` (~4849-4863).
- `src/core/rng.ts` — `randomSeed()` / `createSeededRng()` (`Math.random`-seeded runs by default).
- `src/test/gameHarness.ts` — `bootScene`/`advanceGame` deterministic harness (frame-loop stop/resume behaviour).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `_resolvePlayerBulletsVsEnemies` (~1189) and `onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy` (~384) — read-only context for the interference analysis.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** no gameplay defect is being masked. If the isolated test still fails for a fixed seed, the flake may reflect a real horde/accounting bug — escalate as a new (child) work item instead of widening the tick.
- **Risk:** adding `scene.setRng(...)` in this describe block changes the RNG stream for the other four horde tests in the same block; keep the seed pinned in a `beforeEach`-style helper or per-test so assertions like "spawns the configured horde" stay valid.
- **Risk:** a bounded tick loop can hide a regression that makes kills take longer; keep the bound small (≈ 0.32 s simulated) and assert exactly-once accounting afterwards.
- **Risk (scope creep):** other single-tick kill tests in the same file (asteroids, boss phases) use `tick(0.016)` and have not flaked; do not refactor them wholesale — record as separate work if desired.
- **Risk:** flake attribution — a green re-run under load is weak evidence; the fix must be justified by a *reproduced deterministic* failure, not by "it passed 20 times".
- **Risk:** `isolateEnemyForKill` stubs `getEnemyEntities` and `autoFireEnabled` on the instance and must be restored in a `finally` block (as the pursuer test does); a leaked stub would silently affect later tests in the same file.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK** (completed) — `[test-failure] PlayScene — flaky wave-accounting kill tests (Harvester + Pac-Man pursuer)`; introduced `isolateEnemyForKill` for exactly this interference class. Direct precedent.
- **AH-0MUNVVWWC0015JTM** (completed) — `Flaky tests: PlayScene and GymFormationScene fail intermittently under full-suite parallel load`; load-sensitivity remediation (deterministic boot/frames).
- **AH-0MV5JRAH90034PKR** (completed) — `Flaky Centipede chain bounds assertion under full-suite load`; fixed "advanced 20 s in one tick" by stepping in 0.05 s increments — precedent for tick-size fixes in this file.
- **AH-0MVFPMT4P005UHZL** — removed the last wall-clock waits from the suites (`advanceGame` / `stepGameUntil`); the deterministic harness this test relies on.
- **AH-0MV01EKTL001NRE6** — the Robotron homing horde feature these tests cover.
- **AH-0MVLJFCE6007T77H** (completed) — docs-only change whose gate surfaced this flake (`discovered-from`).
- `src/test/wallClockWaitGuard.test.ts` — repo guard documenting the flake history and the supported deterministic replacements.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (agent consideration):** "Is the failure load-induced (wall-clock frame drift) or seed-induced (random horde layout)?"
  - **Answer (resolved from repo evidence, no producer input needed):** seed-induced is demonstrable from the code — `bootWithHordeWave` injects no RNG, so `_initRunSeed()` draws `randomSeed()` per run and `computeHordeSpawns` places grunts at RNG-jittered edge positions. The pass-on-re-run therefore used a different layout. Load may additionally drift scene state via live RAF frames before `advanceGame` stops the loop, but that is not required to explain the flake. Source: `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:4849-4863`, `src/core/rng.ts:49`, `src/waves/HordeSpawner.ts` (`computeHordeSpawns`).
- **Q (agent consideration):** "Does the description's proposed fix (`scene.tick(0.05)` / tick-until-dead) actually address the mechanism?"
  - **Answer (resolved from repo evidence):** only partially. `scene.tick(dt)` is synchronous, so "the collision step did not process the projectile" cannot happen; the pursuer precedent (AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK) shows the real interference was auto-fire / overlapping entities, fixed by `isolateEnemyForKill`. The brief therefore requires isolation (plus a fixed seed) as the primary fix, with a bounded tick loop only as a secondary robustness measure.
- **Q (agent consideration):** "Should the fix change gameplay code (e.g. horde collision ordering)?"
  - **Answer (resolved from repo constraints):** no. Any gameplay change is shared with every gym and would require gym-parity work; a genuine defect would be filed as a new work item instead. Assumption recorded in *Risks & assumptions*.
- **Producer input:** none required — the item's goal and acceptance criteria are unambiguous and the remaining decisions are resolved by repo evidence and precedent. Recorded here for auditability; no open questions.

- **AH-0MUIGTRFY002JDDS** – Shared mineral kill-drop helper + PlayScene/BaseEnemy refactor (completed) — touches the same enemy-kill finalisation path.

Satisfies AC1.

Test comment references AH-0MVMEI9V1005H0LU + AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK. Satisfies AC3-AC5.

# We need an outer loop (AH-0MVNSSY9L001P1CC)

## Objective

**User story (producer).** As the producer, I want the region/home-world proposal
plus **two genuinely different** outer-loop candidates, each written up as a
decision-ready outline on the same footing, so that I can choose one and have it
written into the Game Design Document (GDD) with confidence.

**User story (player).** As a player, I want something to carry forward between
runs — a long-term goal and a sense that my play changes the world — so that
losing a run does not mean losing all progress, and so that beating the final
boss is a milestone on the way to winning rather than the end of everything.

## Users

- **Producer / designer (primary).** Chooses one of three outlined loops and owns
  the GDD write-up; needs comparable, honest outlines and a defensible ranking.
- **Player (arcade / bullet-hell fan).** Needs a reason to return after a lost
  run and a goal beyond a high score; wants progress that survives failure.
- **Developer / agent implementing the loop later.** Needs each outline to name
  the systems, seams and gym coverage so the chosen loop can be planned without
  re-deriving the design.

## Problem statement

The game has a strong **inner loop** (flying, dodging formations, destroying
enemies) and a functioning **middle loop** (per-run ship upgrading through
minerals → hold-full power-up choices → levelled weapons), but **no outer loop**:
nothing persists between runs except a leaderboard score, player settings and a
single run checkpoint. A death ends the run outright (GDD §4.6: "There is no
continue mechanic. Game over is final"), so long-term engagement rests entirely
on score chasing. The fiction ("pilot a resistance ship through a digital
underworld ruled by rogue AI") implies a war to be won, but the game currently
has no structure that represents winning it.

The producer has proposed one candidate outer loop (contested regions with a
home world to find and defend) and asked for **two other candidates** to be
brainstormed and outlined, after which the producer chooses one for the GDD.

## Deliverable

A single design-exploration document — `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — built
to the same standard as the existing research catalogues
(`docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md`, `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md`):
selected candidates written up per-concept, a "considered but not selected"
section, and a selection recommendation. It is a **design document only**: no
gameplay code, no persistence schema changes and no new scenes are implemented
in this item.

The producer's choice is then written into the GDD as a follow-on work item; this
item ends at the candidate document, the comparison and the recommendation.

## Loop tiers used by the document

| Tier | Timescale | Definition in this game | Exists today? |
|------|-----------|-------------------------|---------------|
| **Inner** | Seconds | Flying, dodging, destroying enemies and formations within a wave | Yes (GDD §2.3–2.6) |
| **Middle** | Minutes (a run) | Ship upgrading: minerals → hold-full power-up/weapon choices, levelled effects, extra lives | Yes (GDD §4.4, §4.6) |
| **Outer** | Hours (a campaign / a season) | What the player carries **between** runs and what they are ultimately trying to achieve | **No** |

## Candidate A — Contested Regions / Home World (producer's proposal)

Recorded as proposed, not redesigned. Its outline must preserve every named
mechanic:

- Space is divided into **regions**; each region has an **AI aggression level**.
- The ship can **warp a limited distance** to adjacent regions.
- The goal is to find a region with **zero aggression** containing a **planet
  that can become home to the humans**.
- Having found it, the player must **defend all adjacent regions** against
  attack by aggressive AI.
- The player may leave their **fully upgraded ship** in a region with an **AI
  automated pilot** that defends that region.
- The player then returns home and **collects another ship with no upgrades**,
  and must go out again to make it strong enough to be left guarding another
  region.
- **Factional AI warfare** changes region strength over time: warring AI
  factions fight over a region and the winner leaves a stronger force there.
- **Win condition:** all regions have successfully defended against a massive AI
  onslaught, at which point the home world is safe and the game is won.

The outline must state its **minimal first slice** (the smallest version that
proves the loop is fun), because the full proposal is the largest of the three.

## Candidate B — Salvage Fleet (proposed direction, resource-persistent meta)

A **roguelite meta-progression** outer loop that leaves the map alone and
persists **player power** instead.

- Between runs the player spends **banked salvage** (minerals and mini-boss AI
  cores extracted at the existing checkpoint moments) in a persistent **hangar**
  to unlock hulls, starting weapons and permanent modifiers.
- Each run is a **deployment** flown in one chosen hull; losing the run forfeits
  that run's unbanked salvage but never the hangar.
- The outer goal is to assemble a fleet strong enough for a final assault run at
  maximum threat.
- Progression axis: **build/economy** (what the player owns), not territory.

## Candidate C — Signal Decode (proposed direction, knowledge-persistent meta)

A **campaign-mutating** outer loop where the thing that persists is
**information**.

- Mini-bosses and the boss drop **data fragments** that assemble a persistent
  codex revealing the origin of the AI and the "hellscape" it generates.
- Codex knowledge **mutates and unlocks the campaign** (new enemy behaviours,
  hellscape modifiers, shortcuts), and the final confrontation only becomes
  winnable once the core's rules have been decoded — the boss's phases are the
  codex's payoff.
- Progression axis: **knowledge and campaign variation**, not territory or
  currency.

## Required outline structure (every candidate)

1. **Fantasy / pitch** — one paragraph, in the game's fiction.
2. **Loop structure** — moment-to-moment → run → meta, with an explicit
   statement of *what carries between runs*.
3. **States** — win, lose, partial progress and what a bad run still advances.
4. **New systems** required (named, with rough size).
5. **Reuse of existing systems** — checkpoint (`src/core/checkpointStore.ts`),
   minerals/power-up levels, `Leaderboard`, difficulty curves
   (`src/data/difficulty-curves.csv`), mini-boss rewards, bot/attract mode.
6. **Persistence and save model** — a sketch `localStorage` payload under
   §6.6 rules (defensive parse, no backend) with migration note.
7. **Session shape** — target run length and hours-to-win.
8. **UI / scene surface** — which new screens or menu entries are needed.
9. **Gym testability and the bot** — how its gameplay additions can be exercised
   in a gym (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity rule) and how attract mode can complete
   or avoid stalling on the outer loop.
10. **Pillar impact** — which current GDD pillars it changes (e.g. "no continue,
    game over is final", the single final boss), stated explicitly.
11. **Effort and risk** — sized honestly, with the failure modes that would make
    the loop unfun.
12. **Minimal first slice** — the smallest shippable version.

A **comparison table** then ranks all candidates on: fit with the existing
pilots-in-a-digital-hell fiction, reuse of shipped systems, new-system cost,
persistence complexity, session length fit, legibility of progress to the player,
gym/bot testability, and risk of trivialising or gutting the shipped campaign —
followed by an explicit **recommendation with rationale** and why the others rank
lower. A "Considered but not selected" section records further ideas (e.g. an
arcade-style tiered mutator ladder, a pure daily-seed challenge ladder) with a
one-line deferral reason each.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Deliverable exists and frames the problem.** `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`
   exists, opens with the inner/middle/outer tier definitions above and the
   comparison criteria, and states that it is design-only.
2. **Candidate A is complete and faithful.** Candidate A is written up with all
   twelve required sections and preserves every mechanic listed in *Candidate A*
   above (regions, limited warp, per-region aggression, zero-aggression home
   region with a habitable planet, defence of adjacent regions, autonomous-pilot
   ship hand-off, unupgraded replacement ship, faction warfare, all-regions-held
   win). No proposed mechanic is silently dropped, altered or merged.
3. **Two additional candidates, materially distinct.** Candidates B and C each
   carry all twelve required sections and each names *what persists between
   runs* differently from Candidate A and from each other; each is justified
   against at least one named design pillar or fiction element.
4. **Decision-ready comparison.** The document contains a comparison table across
   the agreed criteria, an explicit recommendation with rationale, and a ranked
   justification for why the two non-recommended candidates rank lower.
5. **Alternatives recorded.** A "Considered but not selected" section lists at
   least two further outer-loop ideas with a one-line deferral reason each.
6. **Docs guard test.** A vitest docs-guard test (convention:
   `src/classicPowerUpWeaponResearchDocs.test.ts`) asserts the document exists,
   contains the tier definitions, the comparison table and, for each of the three
   candidates, the twelve required section headings — so the deliverable cannot
   silently regress. It passes in the changed-scope test gate.
7. **Cross-linked, not orphaned.** The new document is cross-linked from the GDD
   future-scope section (§8) and from where the other design catalogues are
   referenced in `README.md`; every added link resolves to a file or anchor that
   exists.
8. **Producer decision is staged, not pre-empted.** The document ends with a
   "Producer decision record" section (candidate | decision | date | notes) left
   pending, plus a note that the chosen loop's GDD write-up is a follow-on work
   item. No GDD gameplay text for the chosen loop is written in this item.
9. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, `README.md`, and the GDD cross-links.
10. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Design only.** No gameplay, persistence-schema or scene implementation in
  this item; each candidate is marked "design only, not scheduled".
- **No backend.** All persistence must fit the existing `localStorage` model
  (GDD §6.6) with defensive parsing, as the leaderboard and checkpoint do.
- **Engine policy.** Candidates must not require a new engine or editor-driven
  content (GDD §6.1: code-first, Phaser).
- **Pillars are explicit, not accidental.** A candidate may propose changing an
  existing pillar (e.g. "no continue", the single final boss) but must say so in
  its *Pillar impact* section with a rationale and a cost.
- **Gym↔game parity.** Any gameplay element a candidate proposes must be
  exercisable in a gym scene, and the outline must say how (AGENTS.md parity

# Player Phase Shift unmistakable treatment

Implementation of the player path for AH-0MVNTR89P0022JIU: aggressive on the
activation edge, soft while sustained, never shaking the camera.

## Goal

As a player relying on the automatic Phase Shift, I want the activation to read
as an unmistakable system event — a flash, a distortion hit and a strong
chromatic surge — then settle into a clearly-visible sustained shimmer, so I can
trust the state and time my flying.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Activation edge (aggressive).** The rising edge fires, in the same frame:
  a widened/stronger chromatic-surge overlay pair, a full-screen flash in a
  phase-shift palette (not the death-flash palette), a cyan edge/vignette band
  layer, and the camera distortion burst from `cameraFilters.ts`.
- **Sustained state (soft).** While phased: the vivid pulsing chromatic split
  (raised alpha and offset with the slow oscillation), the edge/vignette bands
  and the gentle sustained camera filter, all pulsing rather than static;
  sustained flicker stays at or below the documented seizure-safety cap.
- **Exact teardown.** Falling edge removes every overlay, tween and camera
  filter; nothing is left on screen or in the camera filter list.
- **Toggles and tunables.** Each new layer has a `PHASE_SHIFT_ENABLE_*` toggle
  and every magnitude is an exported constant; disabling a layer leaves the rest
  working.
- **No shake.** `camera.shake` is never called (regression test retained).
- **Headless safe.** Without a render context the controller still constructs
  and updates as a no-op.
- **Tests.** The sibling test contract item passes.
- Player activation edge is an aggressive, structural glitch: a short camera-filter distortion burst plus a full-screen phase flash plus a wider chromatic surge. (implemented here)
- Player sustained state stays continuously obvious but soft: pulsing vivid split, cyan edge vignette bands, gentle sustained camera filter, no camera shake. (implemented here)
- Exact teardown: the falling edge removes every overlay, tween and camera filter, restoring the camera filter list with no residual state or duplicate layer. (implemented here)

# Bot tuning scene is not using the same gameplay objects as the main game

## Problem statement

Gym scenes are the canonical parity reference for the shipped game, yet the
level-launch gym path (`GymLevel`, which `GymBotTuning` extends) carries its own
inline wave-spawn implementation that has drifted from `PlayScene`. A designer
tuning the bot therefore watches enemies that do **not** behave as they do in
play, which invalidates the tuning signal the gym exists to provide.

## Findings from repo investigation (intake, 2026-10-27)

The reported symptom is real and is one of several divergences in the same spawn
seam:

1. **Phasers spawn in a line then snap to their ring (reported bug).**
   `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:1647`) and
   `GymFormationScene` (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts:1755`) both
   resolve an orbital entity's wormhole-transit destination through the entity's
   live `formationSlot()` seam (AH-0MVEXVME1004SIIS). `GymLevel.spawnWave`
   (`src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts:299`) does not: its resolver returns the grid
   slot (`startX + driftX + col * spacingX`), so Phasers transit to a straight
   line and then snap onto the orbit when the spawn window ends. Because
   `GymBotTuning extends GymLevel` (`src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts:149`), the
   bot-tuning gym reproduces exactly the symptom the producer reported.
   Regression coverage exists for `PlayScene`
   (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:6697`) and `GymFodderEnemies`
   (`src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.test.ts:396`) but **not** for
   `GymLevel`/`GymBotTuning`.

2. **Launched-level enemies never fire.** `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` assigns
   `entity.shootEnabled = spawn.shootEnabled`; `GymLevel.spawnWave` never
   assigns it, and `BaseEnemy._shootEnabled` defaults to `false`
   (`src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts:97`), so every `tryFire*` method returns nothing.
   Campaign levels 4+ carry `shootEnabled: true`
   (`src/waves/Formations.ts:157`), so a level launched from the curve editor or
   played in the bot-tuning gym is silently non-threatening. `GymLevel`'s own
   tests work around this by setting `victim.shootEnabled = true` by hand
   (`src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.test.ts:599`), which is itself evidence of the gap.

3. **March formations do not march.** `PlayScene` keeps a rigid `marchState`
   block and re-anchors march spawns (`_resetMarchFormation`,
   `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:1737`); `GymLevel` has only horizontal `driftX`.
   Campaign levels 2–10 contain `march` groups
   (`src/waves/Formations.ts:381-424`), so the launched block renders as a
   static line instead of the stepping/dropping block the game shows.

4. **The transit resolver is copied three times.** Each spawn site inlines the
   same non-trivial logic ("autonomous-mover exemption → orbital-slot branch →
   live slot / offset fallback"). The repo-wide duplicate-body guard
   (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, `EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS`)
   does not cover this seam, which is why the third copy could drift unnoticed.
   `GymLevel` also keeps a legacy in-place spawn path used when no wormhole
   origin is supplied — dead for gameplay but still a second code path to keep
   honest.

5. **Divergences that must be preserved (already documented).** `GymPlayer`'s
   obstacle course, `GymWeapons`' AOE training targets, the flat supply cadence
   in `GymFormationScene`-derived gyms, gym-only HUD/tuning panels and the
   absence of run telemetry are intentional and recorded in
   `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 and `docs/BALANCING.md`. The
   fix must not "unify" these away.

## Users and example user stories

- **Bot-tuning designer (primary):** "As a designer tuning the bot in
  `GymBotTuning`, I want the enemies I watch to spawn, transit, march and fire
  exactly as they do in the shipped game, so the tuning I save transfers to the
  attract demo and recordings."
- **Gameplay developer:** "As a developer landing a spawn/formation fix in
  `PlayScene`, I want the gyms to consume the same seam, so I cannot leave a gym
  behind without the test suite failing."
- **Level/curve designer:** "As a designer launching a campaign level from the
  curve editor, I want the launched level to be a faithful preview of the
  shipped level."

## Existing state

- Three spawn implementations: `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` (game),
  `GymFormationScene` (formation gyms), `GymLevel.spawnWave` (level/bot-tuning
  gyms). Only the first two honour the `formationSlot` seam.
- Spawn presentation (`startSpawnAnimation`, wormhole open/close, spawn
  protection) is already shared via `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts`; what diverges is
  the **destination resolver**, the per-enemy `shootEnabled` hand-off and the
  march block.
- Gym↔game parity coverage is extensive for combat, drops, movement, boss
  motion and projectile lifecycle, but has no coverage for the start-of-wave
  spawn presentation on the level-launch path.
- The capture/scripted-scene seam (`src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts`) is already
  consumed by `GymFormationScene` and `GymLevel` only, and the scene registry
  (`scripts/capture-scenes.mjs`) already lists every `Gym<Name>` as capturable
  except the parameterised `GymFodderEnemies`/`GymLevel`.

## Desired change

1. Extract the wormhole-transit destination resolution into **one** shared
   helper under `src/scenes/core/` and make all four spawn sites
   (`PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel`, `GymBoss` minions) consume it,
   so the orbital-slot seam, the autonomous-mover exemption and the live-slot
   tracking can no longer drift.
2. Propagate the wave's per-enemy `shootEnabled` (and the formation RNG) through
   the `GymLevel` spawn path exactly as `PlayScene` does.
3. Bring the march block to the level-launch path (or consume the shared march
   state) so launched march waves step and drop as they do in the game.
4. Register the new seam in the duplicate-body guard and add cross-scene
   equivalence tests that boot `PlayScene` and `GymLevel`/`GymBotTuning` with the
   same seeded orbital/march wave and assert identical spawn trajectories and
   identical fire cadence.
5. Sweep **every** gym scene (`src/scenes/gym/`, including the generic
   `GymFormationScene` and the level/bot-tuning path) against `PlayScene` for
   enabled-object parity and record the result in a single parity matrix. **Fix
   every real divergence found in this item** (each with a test), rather than
   deferring them; documented, intentional divergences stay, with their reason
   recorded in the matrix.
6. Adopt the scripted-scene `setup` seam in **every** gym in this item: each gym
   applies the shared `applySceneSetup` applier and exposes whatever

# Scripted scenes for video (excitement-curve scene arc)

**Headline:** Author the example scripted-video scene list — a seven-scene excitement-curve arc (maxed-out opener → humble beginnings → escalating encounters → mini-boss → reprise → final boss) rendered by `npm run capture:scenes` — backed by a small dev-gated setup extension so weapon levels 2–5, the Hull Full reward, and the mini-boss/boss deaths are deterministic on camera, replacing `examples/scenes.json` and recorded once end-to-end.

## Problem statement

The capture pipeline (`npm run capture:scenes -- --config scenes.json`) can already compile any scene list into one video with 0.25 s cross-fades, and the current example (`examples/scenes.json`) demonstrates the schema with a generic showcase. What is missing is **the actual example video content for a scripted, narrative arc**: a scene list whose content deliberately rises in excitement — from a visually loaded opening, through an under-powered early scene, to escalating enemy pressure and two boss pay-offs, each beat ending on a definite on-camera outcome. The scene-capture `setup` seam cannot yet express the specific beats the arc demands: weapons starting above level 1, a guaranteed Hull Full reward, and a mini-boss/boss that dies inside the capture window.

**User story:** As the maintainer, I want a ready-to-run example scene config for the scripted video that follows the agreed excitement curve — opening on a fully upgraded, heavily-outfought spectacle, then dropping to a humble early scene and building back up through escalating encounters to a mini-boss and the main boss — so a recorded showcase video tells a satisfying arc instead of a flat sequence, and each scene's ending (Hull Full reward, mini-boss death, boss death) lands on camera.

## Users

- **Primary — the maintainer / release owner.** Wants the example scripted video to demonstrate the game's range (from bare-cannon play to a fully-upgraded arsenal) in one ~60–75 s showcase cut, with deterministic outcomes so the recording reproduces the intended arc.
- **Secondary — prospective players / viewers.** The audience of the showcase: they should read a clear difficulty/excitement curve and understand the game's progression fantasy (starting weak, ending gloriously overpowered).

**Example user stories:**
- As the maintainer, I can run one command against the shipped example config and get the compiled arc video, so my demo footage follows the designed curve rather than a flat generic sequence.
- As the maintainer, I can tweak a number in the config (a weapon level, an enemy count, a seed) and re-record, trusting the rest of the arc and the on-camera endings to stay in place.
- As a viewer, I see each scene's payoff (Hull Full, mini-boss death, boss death) actually happen on screen, so the video reads as scripted rather than accidental.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — The seven-scene arc is authored as the example config.** `examples/scenes.json` is replaced by the excitement-curve arc in the exact beat order: (1) **Opening spectacle** — many enemies, lots of minerals and upgrades, all six upgrade slots filled with weapons at levels 2–5; (2) **Humble origins** — default weapon only, the wormhole spawns a few weak enemies, many asteroids to destroy and collect, ending with the player receiving the **Hull Full** reward; (3) **First steps up** — about 2× the enemies of scene 2, 3 weapon slots filled at level 1; (4) **Escalation** — 2× the enemies of scene 3, 5 slots filled at levels 1–2; (5) **Mini-boss** — a reasonable escort of enemies, all slots filled at levels 1–3, ending with the **mini-boss death**; (6) **Reprise** — similar pressure to scene 4, different enemies, more (stronger) player weapons; (7) **Main boss** — a heavy loadout, ending with the **boss death**. Each entry carries `target`, `playMs`, `captureMs`, `label` and the `setup` that realises its beat; the file passes the existing pre-boot scene-config validation unchanged.
- [ ] **AC2 — Deterministic arc beats via a small dev-gated setup extension.** The scene `setup` seam (`src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts` → gyms) gains, with validated/normalised support in `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` (+ `.d.mts` types and error codes): (a) `player.weaponLevels` — per-weapon permanent levels 2–5 (existing `player.weapons` stays the level-1 grant path); (b) `setup.bossHitsRemaining` — the boss gyms (`GymBoss`, `GymMiniBoss`) spawn their entity with that many hits left (its `initialHp`), precedent `PlayScene.startDevBossScenario(bossHitsRemaining)` and the gyms' on-screen DAMAGE seams; (c) `setup.mineralReward` — the hold-full choice in the level gyms resolves to that reward id, so scene 2's Hull Full pay-off is deterministic. Each new field is validated, normalised and documented alongside the existing ones. The extension is dev-gated/inert for production: `npm run check-bundle` stays green and the gym↔game parity suite (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) stays green; no shipped-game gameplay behaviour changes.
- [ ] **AC3 — The recorded video verifies the arc and endings.** One end-to-end run — `npm run capture:scenes -- --config examples/scenes.json` — produces a single playable WebM (git-ignored `capture-output/…` or explicit `--output`), with the expected scene count, all fade probes passing (250 ms fades verified as dark), and the three scripted pay-offs (Hull Full resolution, mini-boss death, boss death) visible in their scenes' windows. Scene count/timings reported in the `--json` payload; the ~60–75 s target is the baseline (longer windows are acceptable where a beat needs them).
- [ ] **AC4 — The arc is seeded and reproducible.** Every setup-bearing scene carries a stable `seed`; re-running the config reproduces the same loadouts and (at the content level — minerals, drops, asteroid plan) the same playfield. The seeds are pinned by the hermetic tests so an author editing the file cannot silently lose determinism.
- [ ] **AC5 — Testing/validation.** Hermetic tests (extending `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts`) cover: parse/validate/normalise/idempotence of the new setup fields, the exact scene-table assertions for the seven beats (targets, loadouts, slot counts, `bossHitsRemaining`, `mineralReward`, seeds), applier tests in `sceneSetup.test.ts` for weapon levels / forced reward, and updated `examples/scenes.json` pins in `src/multiSceneCaptureDocs.test.ts` and `capture-scenes.test.ts` (both presently assert the *old* example's `GymFodderEnemies`/`PlayScene` entries — these expectations are updated to the new arc while keeping their validating intent). Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` documents the new setup fields (`player.weaponLevels`, `bossHitsRemaining`, `mineralReward`), the two-way doc↔schema parity test is updated for them, and the example config is referenced; the README's existing `capture:scenes`/`scenes.json` cross-links remain accurate; code comments updated. (CHANGELOG.md is managed by the ship release pipeline and is excluded.)

## Constraints

- **Dev-gated only.** All scene-config content and the new setup fields are capture/dev tooling: no change to the shipped gameplay bundle (`npm run check-bundle` must stay green) and no new gameplay behaviour in `PlayScene`. The capture director and setups already exist only in dev builds; boss/mini-boss hit-preview is an explicit dev/capture-facing seam (as today's DAMAGE buttons in the gyms already are).
- **Gym↔game parity, no forked gameplay.** The loadout/power-up/seed mapping continues through the one shared `applySceneSetup` applier; gyms never copy game behaviour. The new fields only *configure* state the game already has (permanent weapon grants, `initialHp`, the hold-full choice strategy).
- **Schema single-source.** New setup fields are validated in the pure `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` module, typed in `capture-scenes.d.mts`, and pinned by tests + the docs parity test — one source of truth, no drift.
- **Deterministic where promised.** The three scripted pay-offs and the loadout/level progression are deterministic requirements; everything else (asteroid density, exact drop cadence) is seed-driven best effort documented as such.
- **UK English** in all written output and documentation. Keep changes surgical; report (do not delete) dead code.

## Existing state (verified 2026-10-27 against HEAD)

- Multi-scene capture ships and is documented: `npm run capture:scenes -- --config scenes.json` parses/validates the scene list before any browser boots, drives one continuous `MediaRecorder` across all scenes via the dev-gated in-page director (`window.__aiHellCaptureDirector`), and inserts 250 ms fade-to/from-black between scenes (`SCENE_FADE_MS`, `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs`).
- `examples/scenes.json` is the generic showcase example: `GymPlayer`/`GymWeapons`/`GymPowerUpsCombat`, a `PlayScene` generated-level entry, one `GymLevel` setup, one `GymFodderEnemies` setup, and `GymBoss` — pinned by `src/multiSceneCaptureDocs.test.ts` and `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts`.
- The scene `setup` seam (AH-0MVNW8VNN004FFK1) supports `level.waves[].groups[]` (enemyKey/formation/count/spacing), `startWave`, `player.weapons` (permanent, each granted **level 1**), `powerUps` (arbitrary levels), and `seed`. It is applied through the shared `applySceneSetup` so every gym (incl. `GymLevel`, `GymMiniBoss`, `GymBoss` via `GymFormationScene.init/create`) maps a setup to play state identically.
- `GymLevel` plays like the game: wormhole wave spawns, the shared asteroid hazard, the real mineral/drop supply layer, and the 30 s wave window — so authored levels reproduce game behaviour. A full mineral hold resolves automatically to one random reward in gyms (no modal, keeps the bot playing) — the seam a forced Hull Full reward hooks into.
- The good-boss/death precedent exists dev-gated in `PlayScene.startDevBossScenario(hitsRemaining)` (falls straight into the final boss phase with N hits left; `?scenario=boss&bossHits=N`). Boss phases are 50 hits each (200 total for the main boss); the mini-boss is 5 per phase × 3.
- Gym scene windows are recorded with **no player input**: the ship auto-fires from its spawn and does not move during a scene. Scene design must therefore bring the action to the ship (formation drift, wormhole/asteroid hazards, `mineral_scoop`/`magnet` pulling minerals and drops onto the ship) for the beats that read as "playing".

## Desired change

- **AC1 — The seven beats are present in this exact order**, each entry carrying `target`, `playMs`, `captureMs`, `label` and the `setup` that realises its beat:
  1. **Opening spectacle** — many enemies, lots of minerals/upgrades, all six upgrade slots filled with weapons at levels 2-5.
  2. **Humble origins** — default weapon only, wormhole spawns a few weak enemies, many asteroids, ending on the **Hull Full** reward (`setup.mineralReward`).
  3. **First steps up** — about 2x scene 2's enemies, 3 weapon slots filled at level 1.
  4. **Escalation** — about 2x scene 3's enemies, 5 slots filled at levels 1-2.
  5. **Mini-boss** — reasonable escort, all slots filled at levels 1-3, ending on the **mini-boss death** (`setup.bossHitsRemaining`).
  6. **Reprise** — pressure similar to scene 4, **different enemies**, more (and stronger) player weapons than scene 4.
  7. **Main boss** — heavy loadout, ending on the **boss death** (`setup.bossHitsRemaining`).

# Shared wormhole-transit destination seam, consumed by all four spawn sites

Parent: AH-0MVP5IGX5005XTVV (AC4, and prerequisite for AC1). **Pure refactor: behaviour must not
change in any scene.**

## Goal / user story

As a gameplay developer, I want the wormhole-transit destination resolution defined exactly once,
so that the game and every gym consume the same "autonomous-mover exemption → orbital live slot →
grid-slot/offset fallback" rule, and a re-introduced copy fails the suite.

## Problem

The resolver is currently inlined three times:

- `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:1647`) — the reference behaviour
  (`formationSlot` seam + `marchState` base + `driftX`).
- `GymFormationScene._spawnFormation` (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts:1755`) — same
  rule, portal-based base, no march.
- `GymLevel.spawnWave` (`src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts:299`) — a **divergent** copy that returns the
  grid slot and therefore reproduces the reported "Phaser spawns in a line then snaps" symptom.
- `GymBoss` minion spawn (`src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts:274`) — no resolver at all (in-place).

The repo-wide duplicate-body guard (`EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS` in
`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) does not cover this seam, which is why the third
copy could drift unnoticed.

## Desired change

1. New module `src/scenes/core/spawnTransit.ts` exporting **one** resolver, e.g.
   `resolveSpawnTransitTarget(...)`, which takes the narrow structural inputs it needs and returns
   `{ x, y }` or `undefined` (meaning "no transit — spawn in place"):
   - the entity (read structurally for `autonomousPositioning` and optional `formationSlot`);
   - the base position for this frame (march base when the wave is a march block, else
     `startX + driftX`, `startY`);
   - the formation `offset` and the group `spacingX` / `spacingY`.
   The resolver owns the rule only — it must not import Phaser, must not read scene fields, and must
   not mutate the entity.
2. Consume it at **all four** spawn sites. Each site keeps its own *base* computation (the game's
   `marchState`, the formation gym's portal, the level gym's launched drift, the boss's in-place
   exemption) — that is scene structure, not the rule.
3. `GymLevel` consumes the seam with **unchanged** behaviour in this item (it will still pass its
   grid-slot base, because it has no march/formation-slot wiring yet); the behaviour fix lands in
   the follow-up `GymLevel` parity item. This keeps this item a verifiable no-op refactor.
4. Register the resolver in `EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS` in
   `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` with the canonical definer path, and extend the
   guard fixture so a re-introduced copy is proven to fail (the guard already has a
   "detects a re-introduced duplicate" describe block to extend).

## Implementation guidance

- Keep the ordering of the existing rule exactly: **autonomous → orbital live slot → grid offset**.
  The orbital branch must call `formationSlot.call(entity, baseX, baseY)` so the entity's own
  geometry stays authoritative (AH-0MVF4P31M0033RAC, AH-0MVEXVME1004SIIS).
- Preserve every existing comment's intent by moving the rationale into the new module's header
  (the "never appear in a line then snap onto the ring" reason) and leaving short pointers at the
  four call sites.
- Prefer a structural input type over importing entity classes, so the module stays pure and the
  gyms can pass their own shapes.
- Do not "fix" the `GymLevel` behaviour here; the red-before tests from the parity-test item must
  still fail after this item lands.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — `src/scenes/core/spawnTransit.ts` exists, is Phaser-free (importable in a node-only
  unit test), and defines the transit destination rule exactly once.
- [ ] AC2 — `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel` and `GymBoss` all resolve their transit
  destination through that single helper; no site re-implements the orbital/autonomous/offset
  branch chain.
- [ ] AC3 — The helper is registered in `EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS` in
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, the single-definer guard passes, and the
  guard's duplicate-detection fixture covers the new helper.
- [ ] AC4 — Unit tests for the new helper cover: autonomous mover → `undefined`; orbital entity →
  live `formationSlot` result (including a slot that differs from the grid slot); non-orbital
  entity → grid slot from base + offset × spacing; march base vs drift base input handling.
- [ ] AC5 — Every pre-existing test passes unchanged (no behaviour change): scene behaviour is
  identical before and after the refactor, verified by the existing PlayScene, GymFormationScene,
  GymBoss and GymLevel suites plus the equivalence suite.
- [ ] AC6 — The red-before parity tests added by AH-0MVRMHJZS001Z6CX still fail after this item
  (proving the refactor alone does not "fix" the bug).

- AC4 — The spawn-transit destination logic is defined exactly **once** repo-wide, is registered in `EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS`, and every spawn site (`PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel`, `GymBoss`) resolves to it; the duplicate-body guard fails if a copy is re-introduced. — **contribution:** this item delivers it in full (see Parent AC coverage below).

## Key files

- `src/scenes/core/spawnTransit.ts` (new) and `src/scenes/core/spawnTransit.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (`_spawnEnemy`)
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` (`_spawnFormation`)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts` (`spawnWave`)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` (minion spawn)
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` (`EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS` + guard fixture)

## Constraints

- No behaviour change in any scene; this item is reviewed as a refactor.
- No balance change.
- Must not touch the documented intentional divergences (obstacle course, AOE targets, flat
  formation-gym supply cadence, gym HUD, no telemetry).

## Parent AC coverage (traceability)

This child contributes to parent AH-0MVP5IGX5005XTVV. The seam extraction guarantees the single-definition requirement of this AC across all four spawn sites.

Parent acceptance criteria satisfied (restated verbatim from the parent brief):

- **Parent AC4 — The spawn-transit destination logic is defined exactly **once** repo-wide, is registered in `EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS`, and every spawn site (`PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel`, `GymBoss`) resolves to it; the duplicate-body guard fails if a copy is re-introduced.**
